description:
The Bhed Palan Yojana is a significant welfare scheme launched by the Government of India aimed at promoting sheep and goat rearing among the rural population.

The scheme was initiated in the year 2019 under the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

It is part of a broader strategy to enhance the livelihood opportunities for the rural poor and to boost the income of farmers.

The primary objective of the Bhed Palan Yojana is to increase the population of sheep and goats in the country.

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to farmers for the purchase of high-quality breeding animals.

The government has set a target to increase the sheep population by 10 percent by the year 2025.

The scheme also aims to improve the quality of wool and meat production in India.

Under this scheme, the government provides a subsidy of up to 50 percent on the cost of purchasing breeding sheep and goats.

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at INR 2,000 per animal.

Farmers can avail of this subsidy for a maximum of 20 animals per beneficiary.

This means that a farmer can receive a total subsidy of up to INR 40,000.

The Bhed Palan Yojana is particularly beneficial for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

These groups are provided with an additional subsidy of 10 percent.

This increases their total subsidy to 60 percent of the purchase cost.

The eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a resident of India and being involved in sheep or goat farming.

Farmers must be at least 18 years old to apply for the scheme.

There is no upper age limit specified for eligibility.

The annual income of the applicant should not exceed INR 1.5 lakh.

The applicant must also possess a valid identification proof and address proof.

To apply for the Bhed Palan Yojana, farmers must follow a specific application process.

The first step is to visit the official website of the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

Farmers need to fill out the application form available on the website.

The application form requires details such as the applicant's name, address, income, and the number of animals to be purchased.

Farmers must also submit documents such as Aadhar card, income certificate, and proof of land ownership.

Once the application is completed, it must be submitted to the local veterinary officer.

The local veterinary officer will verify the application and the submitted documents.

After verification, the application is forwarded to the district animal husbandry department.

The district department will then process the application and approve the subsidy.

The subsidy amount is disbursed directly to the bank account of the beneficiary.

The timeline for the application process can vary.

Generally, the entire process from application submission to subsidy disbursement can take up to 30 days.

The frequency of the scheme's implementation is annual.

Farmers can apply for the subsidy every year based on their needs.

The implementing authority for the Bhed Palan Yojana is the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The scheme is executed through the state animal husbandry departments.

Each state has its own designated officers to assist farmers with the application process.

Farmers can contact the local animal husbandry department for any queries related to the scheme.

The contact details for the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying can be found on their official website.

The Bhed Palan Yojana also aims to promote sustainable livestock farming practices.

The scheme encourages farmers to adopt modern techniques in sheep and goat rearing.

Farmers are provided with training and resources to improve their farming practices.

The government conducts workshops and seminars to educate farmers about best practices in animal husbandry.

The Bhed Palan Yojana has the potential to create significant employment opportunities in rural areas.

By promoting sheep and goat farming, the scheme can help reduce rural poverty.

It also aims to enhance the nutritional security of rural households through increased meat and milk production.

The initiative is expected to contribute to the overall economic development of the rural sector.

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by the year 2022.

The Bhed Palan Yojana is part of the larger National Livestock Mission.

The National Livestock Mission was launched in 2014 with the aim of promoting sustainable livestock development.

The mission focuses on improving livestock productivity and enhancing the income of farmers.

The Bhed Palan Yojana specifically targets small and marginal farmers.

These farmers often face challenges in accessing quality breeding stock.

The scheme aims to bridge this gap by providing financial assistance.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 200 crore for the implementation of the Bhed Palan Yojana.

This budget is intended to cover the subsidy amounts and training programs for farmers.

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders in the agriculture sector.

Farmers have reported increased income levels due to the financial assistance provided.

The Bhed Palan Yojana is expected to play a crucial role in achieving self-sufficiency in meat production.

It also aims to enhance the quality of wool produced in India.

The scheme is expected to benefit over 1 lakh farmers across the country in its initial phase.

The government is committed to monitoring the progress of the scheme regularly.

This includes assessing the impact on farmers' livelihoods and the overall sheep population.

The Bhed Palan Yojana represents a significant step towards improving the socio-economic conditions of rural farmers.

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to supporting the agricultural sector.

It aims to empower farmers by providing them with the necessary resources and knowledge.

The Bhed Palan Yojana is a comprehensive initiative that addresses multiple aspects of livestock farming.

It is designed to create a sustainable and profitable sheep and goat farming sector in India.
